content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List the project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any ageing/humidity or radiator performance documents identified. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates, any documented transparency-loss values after the 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test, and allowed/recommended thickness-related constraints."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard ageing constraint using the extracted document values: eliminate any candidate with transparency loss greater than 10%, and record the numeric transparency-loss values for all candidates for later comparison."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each remaining ageing-qualified radiator candidate, run simulate_separation at thicknesses 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm, recording each numeric pion/kaon separation result at 10 GeV/c."},{"id":"s4","description":"If the best simulated result among the 1 cm grid points for an ageing-qualified candidate is near an endpoint or if more precision is needed, run additional simulate_separation tests at selected intermediate thicknesses within 1–6 cm around the best-performing region for that candidate, and record the numeric results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all recorded simulations for candidates satisfying the ageing constraint, discard any radiator-thickness option with separation below 3.5 sigma, and identify the option with the highest pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c. Provide the selected radiator and thickness, along with its separation and transparency-loss values, for the reporting module’s final recommendation."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Radiator-R1","thickness_cm":2.75,"justification":"Radiator-R1 at 2.75 cm gives the best simulated pion/kaon separation found in the recorded scan/refinement: 4.785 sigma at 10 GeV/c. This exceeds the hard 3.5 sigma requirement and is higher than the best recorded separations for R2 and R3. All three candidates passed the recorded 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing requirement; R1's documented transparency change was recorded as -1%, which is within the maximum allowed 10% loss.
